venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: How Florida’s line led the run against FAU, and why two deep safeties turned into a 90-play night.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — film session from full SEC broadcast. Fan rail empty until Charles approves.
headline: Faulkner kept changing who led Baugh. White left the short throw open.

offense.body:
Most of Saturday, Florida’s run game started from the same picture. Aaron Philo lined up in the shotgun — five yards behind the center — and handed the ball to Jadan Baugh. All five offensive linemen stepped in one direction. Two of them put their hands on the same FAU defensive tackle and drove him, then one of those two left that block and went upfield to pick up a linebacker. Baugh waited a beat, found the opening, and hit it. Florida’s first run after DJ Coleman’s interception was that play: Baugh, up the middle, nine yards from the 6. Faulkner came back to it on first down all night.

Faulkner also put Philo under center on short yardage. Second quarter, fourth-and-1 at Florida’s 49, Florida already up 24–14. Philo put his hands on the center’s hip and sneaked for four yards. That is a sneak. It is not the everyday run.

When FAU’s linebackers started chasing those same-direction runs, Faulkner used the cheat. Four linemen still stepped toward one sideline — call it the left — so FAU’s linebackers ran left with them. The remaining guard, the one on the right, the side the line was stepping away from, pulled out of his stance and ran right so he could lead Baugh through the hole those linebackers had just emptied. If you chased the four linemen, you ran away from the football.

Baugh’s longest run of the night was not a longer version of that everyday run. It was a different play. Third-and-2 in the third quarter, Florida at its own 33, needing two yards. The tight end on the left blocked FAU’s defensive end and held him inside, toward the middle of the field. Florida’s left tackle did not stay and help on that block. He ran around the tight end and became Baugh’s lead blocker on the edge. Baugh stepped toward the left sideline, followed that tackle, broke an arm tackle, and ran 61 yards to FAU’s 6. Two plays later he scored from there.

Faulkner also sent a tight end or an H-back — the extra big body lined up next to the tackle — across the formation after the snap. That player’s job was to block the defensive end on the back side, the end Baugh was running away from. If that end is occupied, Baugh can stop and cut back. On other snaps Faulkner left that end unblocked on purpose. Philo and Baugh held the ball together for a beat. If the end crashed on Baugh, Philo was supposed to pull it and run the empty edge himself. Philo tried that once on the opening drive and lost two yards because FAU’s Enyce Sledge stayed in his gap. The design was sound. The play lost.

Before the snap, Faulkner often sent a receiver walking from one side of the field to the other. That is a test. If an FAU defender ran with that receiver, Florida knew FAU was playing man — each defender has a man. If the defender stayed put, Florida knew FAU was playing zone — each defender has an area. The next call was built off the answer.

The passing game is attached to those runs. Philo faked a handoff, which made the linebackers step up to stop Baugh, then threw to the tight end in the space those linebackers just left. Or he faked the handoff, rolled the opposite way of the fake, and hit a tight end who leaked into the flat — the short area near the sideline, a few yards past the line of scrimmage. Or he did not fake at all. He threw the ball immediately to a receiver a few yards in front of him, and the tackles and guards released downfield to block. Bailey Stockton’s first-quarter touchdown was that play. The linemen were already out in front of him. The throw was a step late. He still walked it in from the 12.

On the opening touchdown drive, Philo threw Dallas Wilson along the left sideline for 19 yards. When FAU’s corners lined up eight yards off the receiver, Philo threw the short stop-route — the receiver takes three steps and turns back to the ball — and the throw to the sideline. Vernell Brown III’s 49-yard touchdown started as a short throw to the right. The first FAU defender missed. Brown was already running. After FAU scored to make it 17–7, Philo threw it over the top to TJ Abrams. Abrams caught it and ran to the 8 — 63 yards.

Philo lined up once with Baugh directly behind him, the old pistol look. Florida ran it one time. It is not becoming the offense.

The offensive line played a clean game — almost no penalties, no late-shift disaster. The twenty-yard loss inside the 5 was not a missed block. Jake Moore snapped the ball over Philo’s head. That is the play that loses real games. Philo ran the offense the rest of the night. When he held the ball too long, the play died. The interception was Micah Mays Jr. — the ball came off his hands, and FAU’s Jayden Sweeney was sitting there.
bullets: Everyday run: Philo in the shotgun, the whole line steps one way, two linemen double a tackle, one climbs to the linebacker, Baugh hits the hole.
Counter: four linemen step left so the linebackers chase left; the right guard pulls right and leads Baugh into the hole they just left.
Third-and-2 in the third quarter, Florida’s 33: tight end holds the end inside, left tackle leads Baugh around him, 61 yards to the 6. Then Baugh scores from there.

defense.body:
Brad White put four linemen on the line of scrimmage and an extra defensive back on the field to match FAU’s third receiver. Two linebackers stood about five yards off the ball. The two safeties stood 12 to 15 yards deep. The corners started 7 to 8 yards off their receivers.

That alignment is a choice. The two deep safeties take away the throw over the top. The corners being that far off means the five-to-eight yard throw is open. FAU never huddled. Caden Veltkamp stood in the shotgun and threw that short ball to Dom Henry and Kelby Valsin over and over. Florida ran 90 plays on defense because those throws kept moving the chains. Jon Sumrall said it after the game: on third-and-1, your corner cannot be nine yards off the receiver. That happened.

White rushed four most snaps. He would walk both linebackers up into the gaps in front of the center so it looked like six men were coming. At the snap those linebackers dropped into coverage. Veltkamp would throw the middle, and a linebacker was already standing there. That is how you get pressure in the quarterback’s head without sending extra rushers. The real extra rusher showed up on short yardage — a defensive back coming free off the edge. Florida also crossed two interior linemen so one tackle came through clean and Veltkamp had to throw the ball away.

When FAU got inside the 10, the safeties came down to about eight yards and extra bodies packed the middle. Florida stuffed the inside run at the 1 more than once. They still lost the yard. Ethan Ervin scored from a yard out. When the defender on the outside left his spot, Veltkamp ran around him and scored from the 7.

The wins on the tape were the ones where Florida’s defensive backs trusted what they saw. Aaron Chiles and DJ Coleman jumped FAU’s throw-it-now screens and blew them up. On the opening drive, third-and-10, Coleman sold that he was playing the middle of the field. Veltkamp thought the outside receiver was one-on-one. Coleman broke back to the sideline, got over the top of the throw, and intercepted it at Florida’s 5. Later he got a hand on another ball. Dijon Johnson caught that one.

White will live with the short throw if his people tackle it. They did not tackle enough of it. That is why Florida’s defense was on the field for 90 plays. The takeaways still ended drives.
bullets: Safeties 12 to 15 yards deep, corners 7 to 8 yards off: the deep ball is dead, the short throw is open. That is how FAU got to 90 plays.
White walks the linebackers up so it looks like a blitz, then they drop. The real extra rusher is a defensive back off the edge on short yardage.
Opening drive, third-and-10: Coleman sold the middle, then intercepted the outside throw at Florida’s 5.

specials.body: Patrick Durkin made a 53-yard field goal. Florida never punted. FAU’s 18-yard punt set up Florida’s second touchdown.

nextWeek.look: Campbell will throw the short ball and their quarterback, Sixkiller, will run. Florida will still hand it to Baugh and change who is leading him. White has to have people standing where that short throw lands. Jayden Woods has to stay on the outside when Sixkiller keeps it.
